parts.text:
1
A wave has a frequency of 5 GHz.
What is the period of the wave?
A
200 ps
B
2 ns
C
20 ns
D
20 000 µs

hints: Notice the frequency is given as $5 \text{ GHz}$, so first write $5 \text{ GHz}$ in hertz using $1 \text{ GHz} = 10^9 \text{ Hz}$.
Connect frequency $f$ to period $T$ with $T = 1/f$, which will give a very small time in seconds.
Convert your time in seconds to picoseconds and nanoseconds using $1 \text{ ps} = 10^{-12} \text{ s}$ and $1 \text{ ns} = 10^{-9} \text{ s}$, then compare with the four options.
walkthrough: Identify the given quantity: frequency $f = 5 \text{ GHz} = 5 \times 10^9 \text{ Hz}$, where $1 \text{ Hz} = 1 \text{ s}^{-1}$.
State the governing relation for any wave: period and frequency are reciprocals, $T = 1/f$.
Substitute the value with units: $T = 1/(5 \times 10^9 \text{ s}^{-1}) = 0.2 \times 10^{-9} \text{ s} = 2.0 \times 10^{-10} \text{ s}$.
Convert to the small units used in the options: $2.0 \times 10^{-10} \text{ s} = 200 \times 10^{-12} \text{ s} = 200 \text{ ps}$, which is also $0.2 \text{ ns}$.
Match $200 \text{ ps}$ to the list of options. This is option A.

B.explanation: This is 10 times too large, from an error with the $10^9$ for GHz or the $10^{-9}$ for ns.

C.explanation: This is 100 times too large, from treating 5 GHz as $5 \times 10^7 \text{ Hz}$ instead of $5 \times 10^9 \text{ Hz}$.

D.explanation: This equals $0.02 \text{ s}$, which corresponds to 50 Hz, not 5 GHz.
